commits.message:
feat(effects): Effected — a per-cell colour effect over a renderable's finished cells (rich-effects-fxiy.3t3)

src/renderables/effect.ts: Effect (cell colours, row/col/seed, t → colours)
and Effected, a Renderable that measures as its child. Segments are cut
only where colours change; unchanged cells keep their ColorSpec, so the
identity effect is byte-identical. Anchors shift per run, wide glyphs stay
whole, colours are built with ColorSpec.fromRgba. Seeds are FNV-1a of a
caller key and the cell position. docs/effects.md; demo in the colour
studio.

feat(core)!: one easing vocabulary — CSS eases and time phases, replacing RAMP_EASINGS (rich-effects-fxiy.87k) (#285)

* feat(core): one easing vocabulary — CSS eases and time phases, replacing RAMP_EASINGS (rich-effects-fxiy.87k)

src/core/easing.ts: Ease (cubicBezier, steps, EASES by CSS name plus
sine and the legacy step), parseEase, and Phase (once/loop/pingPong,
seconds in, no clock read). ColorRamp and the template ramp take an
Ease; RAMP_EASINGS, RAMP_EASING_NAMES, parseRampEasing and RampEasing
are gone. step keeps its exact behaviour, so every template renders
unchanged; an unknown name now reads "unknown easing".

* fix(core): ramp exactness contract, one step-end, an easing docs page (rich-effects-fxiy.87k)

Review round (high): ColorRamp's contract now says what it does —
eased 0/1 are the stops exactly, step-start jumps as CSS defines it,
overshoot holds the end colors — and a test pins it over every EASES
entry. ColorRamp.easing is now .ease, the binding's argument too, and
parseEase's error reads "unknown ease". step and step-end are one
value. docs/easing.md is the page for the vocabulary; the ramp section
links to it instead of copying the name list.
